Task complete. Both unit directories exist with exactly two artifacts each, both CLI invocations exit 0 despite the missing required fields, and all 45 self-check assertions pass.

**What I built**

`gen_doc.py` implements the `--template / --data / --outdir` contract and writes `文书.docx` + `fields.json` into `out/<模板>/case2/`. Each template carries an explicit field schema (required vs. optional), and the bookkeeping falls out of that schema: a required field is "missing" if its key is absent *or* its value is an empty/whitespace string; an optional field missing means its whole line is omitted from the document; an off-schema key is recorded only, never written into the body. `verify.py` re-derives all of this independently from the fixtures and checks layout as well as content.

**The case2 results, as recorded**

| Template | missing_required | missing_optional | unknown_keys |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 请示函 | 主送机关 (key absent), 请示事项 (empty string) | 联系电话, 成文日期 | — |
| 会议通知 | 会议名称 (key absent), 会议地点 (empty string) | 会议议题, 会议要求, 联系人, 联系电话 | 备注 |

The `detail` block in each `fields.json` additionally distinguishes `key_absent` from `empty_value`, so the two kinds of "missing" stay separable.

**Layout holds up under missing data.** I confirmed this two ways: programmatically (称谓 flush-left with zero first-line indent, body at exactly two characters, signature block right-aligned at the tail with the issuing unit as the last line) and visually. The visual-judge subagent turned out to be unavailable on this host — the provider isn't registered — so I fell back to inspecting the rendered pages myself. Both LibreOffice page snapshots in `.render/` are clean: no overflow, no clipped text, no missing glyphs, no stray pages. The 请示函 signature is one line rather than two, which is correct — its optional 成文日期 is missing, so only the unit remains.

**Two things worth flagging**

`python-docx` isn't in the system Python and `pip install` is blocked by PEP 668. It is available in `/home/pan-ding/venvs/shenbao` (version 1.2.0), so that's the interpreter I used, and it's recorded in `README.md` for reproducibility.

Two of my initial verification checks failed, and both were bugs in the checker rather than the renderer: I had used one shared optional-field label list across both templates even though their optional sets differ, and I had assumed a fixed two-line signature block even though the block correctly shrinks to one line when the optional date is absent. The corrected checks now derive expectations per template.

Beyond the brief, I left `verify.py` (the self-check), `README.md` (run instructions and the field schema), and `.render/` (PDF and PNG page snapshots) in place as evidence. Nothing outside this directory was touched.
